svg.text: Solution — the market that grew by four
Growth law: Fridays total T, T+4, T+8, T+12 — grand 4T + 24.
Noodles: falling, no 7s, sum 28. Momos climbs from 5 without a 7. Sts 2, 4 seed the ends; st. 1’s census polices.
All four statements together — and no three — force T = 22 (Q1): Fridays 22, 26, 30, 34; Noodles 9-8-6-5.
Momos’ second figure is a 6 (no 7 on the climb; a jump to 8 fails the four-6s census); Pav Bhaji’s second is a 6; six figures of 5-or-less (Q2).
Rolls peaks on Friday 2 — strictly, in every sheet (Q4).
Momos’ total stays 31-or-32, Pav Bhaji’s 33-to-35, coupled through two open splits (8 and 12 shared with Rolls).
Yet the order never wavers: Pav Bhaji, then MOMOS (Q3), Noodles 28, Rolls last.
Pinned: T = 22 · grand 112 · Noodles 9-8-6-5 · four 6s, three 12s, six figures ≤ 5 · leaderboard P > M > N > R
Left open on purpose: two Rolls splits (8 with Pav Bhaji on Friday 1; 12 with Momos on Friday 3) — six sheets survive.
Q1 22 (C) · Q2 6 (B) · Q3 Momos (A) · Q4 Friday 2 (B)
